+// --- Workspace source fingerprint (#629) -----------------------------------
+//
+// A reviewer receipt for a `workspace_requires` stage (code-generation) must be
+// bound to the SOURCE STATE the reviewer actually inspected: workspace writes
+// deliberately emit no audit events (aidlc-audit-logger.ts excludes them), so
+// without a binding a post-review source edit leaves the receipt satisfying the
+// completion guard for code nobody re-reviewed. The binding is a git-native
+// content fingerprint: per repo, a `git write-tree` over a TEMPORARY index
+// seeded from HEAD with `git add -A` applied — the exact tracked + untracked
+// (gitignore-respecting) content state, computed without touching the real
+// index or worktree. Reverting an edit restores the original fingerprint
+// (content-addressed), so an undone change does not strand a receipt.
+//
+// Multi-repo: the intent's recorded repo set (intentRepos), each resolved via
+// repoDir(); no recorded repos = the legacy single-repo default (projectDir).
+// Returns null when ANY target dir is not a usable git checkout — callers
+// treat null as "no binding available" and keep today's behaviour (fail-open),
+// which also grandfathers receipts recorded before this shipped.
+
+// The literal directory names that hold AIDLC's own workspace state rather
+// than application source: the record tree, the CLI/IDE workspace shell, Bolt
+// swarm worktrees, and the sensor cache (e.g. the type-check sensor's
+// `.tsbuildinfo`, which a monorepo's per-package tsconfig anchors OUTSIDE the
+// record tree - core/tools/aidlc-sensor-type-check.ts's `sensorsDir`). Matched
+// via `**/<name>/**` pathspec glob magic so a nested occurrence (a monorepo
+// subpackage) is excluded exactly like the workspace root's own copy, not
+// just the top level - a plain pathspec (no glob magic) implicitly prefix-
+// matches as a directory ONLY relative to repoDir, so `aidlc` alone never
+// reaches `services/backend/aidlc`.
+const AIDLC_WORKSPACE_DIR_NAMES = ["aidlc", ".aidlc", ".aidlc-worktrees", ".aidlc-sensors"];
+
+function gitTreeFingerprint(repoDir: string): string | null {
+  if (!isGitRepoDir(repoDir)) return null;
+  const idx = join(
+    tmpdir(),
+    `aidlc-src-fp-${process.pid}-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`,
+  );
+  const env = { ...process.env, GIT_INDEX_FILE: idx };
+  try {
+    // Seed from HEAD so deletions of tracked files change the tree. An unborn
+    // HEAD (fresh init) fails read-tree; the empty temp index is then correct.
+    spawnSync("git", ["-C", repoDir, "read-tree", "HEAD"], { env, encoding: "utf-8" });
+    const add = spawnSync("git", ["-C", repoDir, "add", "-A"], { env, encoding: "utf-8" });
+    if (add.status !== 0) return null;
+    // Drop the aidlc workspace family from the fingerprint, at ANY depth: the
+    // record tree is COMMITTED by design and mutates on every engine action
+    // (the very REVIEW_COMPLETED append this fingerprint is stamped into,
+    // gate rows, state updates), so including it would make every receipt
+    // stale by the time the completion guard recomputes. Record-artifact
+    // freshness is already covered by the audit-event invalidation; this
+    // fingerprint is the APPLICATION SOURCE binding. --ignore-unmatch keeps
+    // this a no-op when nothing matches (sibling repos with no aidlc tree).
+    spawnSync(
+      "git",
+      [
+        "-C", repoDir, "rm", "-r", "-q", "--cached", "--ignore-unmatch", "--",
+        ...AIDLC_WORKSPACE_DIR_NAMES.map((name) => `:(glob)**/${name}/**`),
+      ],
+      { env, encoding: "utf-8" },
+    );
+    const wt = spawnSync("git", ["-C", repoDir, "write-tree"], { env, encoding: "utf-8" });
+    if (wt.status !== 0) return null;
+    const sha = wt.stdout.trim();
+    if (sha.length === 0) return null;
+
+    // A submodule is recorded in the tree above as a gitlink (its checked-out
+    // commit sha), so editing its tracked source WITHOUT committing inside the
+    // submodule leaves the gitlink - and therefore `sha` above - unchanged,
+    // shipping a reviewed-then-edited submodule as if nothing had changed.
+    // Fold each INITIALIZED submodule's own fingerprint (recursive - a
+    // submodule can itself nest submodules) into the parent's. An
+    // uninitialized submodule has no materialized content in the workspace,
+    // so it contributes nothing to bind. Gitlinks are read straight off the
+    // temp index (mode 160000 in `ls-files -s`) rather than via `git submodule
+    // status`, which spawns the submodule subsystem and measured 1s+ per call
+    // on Windows - a cost this fingerprint (recomputed on every completion
+    // route) cannot afford.
+    const lsFiles = spawnSync("git", ["-C", repoDir, "ls-files", "-s"], { env, encoding: "utf-8" });
+    const subLines: string[] = [];
+    if (lsFiles.status === 0) {
+      for (const line of lsFiles.stdout.split("
")) {
+        if (!line.startsWith("160000 ")) continue;
+        const tabIdx = line.indexOf("\t");
+        if (tabIdx === -1) continue;
+        const subPath = line.slice(tabIdx + 1).trim();

**[P2] Parse submodule paths without Git quoting**

With the default `core.quotePath` behavior, `git ls-files -s` quotes and escapes non-ASCII paths. For a submodule such as `vendor/cafe-é`, `subPath` contains Git’s quoted representation, `isGitRepoDir` returns false, and edits inside the submodule are omitted from the fingerprint.

This is reproducible: an uncommitted edit inside that submodule leaves the workspace fingerprint unchanged. Please use `git ls-files -s -z` and parse NUL-delimited entries.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed at b4195e9e — gitlinks are now read via ls-files -s -z (NUL-delimited, quoting disabled) instead of -s. Verified with an accented submodule path (vendor/café-módulo): an uncommitted edit inside it now correctly changes the fingerprint.

[P1] Bind unit receipts to an exact stage attempt

The attempt floor compares second-precision timestamps using `<`. When a prior `UNIT_COMPLETED` and a new attempt’s `STAGE_STARTED` occur in the same second, the old receipt is accepted for the new attempt. I reproduced this directly. Use an exact run-floor/attempt identifier, as the swarm receipt path already does, rather than timestamps alone.

**[BLOCKER] The consumes parser drops entries and inverts `required: false`.**

This regex requires a `- ` prefix on every line, so the dash-less `required: false` continuation line terminates the match after the first `- artifact:` line. Two consequences, both reproduced against the shipped `plugins/test-pro/contributions/construction/build-and-test.md` (two consumes, both `required: false`):

- every entry after the first is dropped, with no recordDrop
- `reqs` is empty, so `reqs[i]?.[1] !== "false"` evaluates true and the author's `required: false` flips to `required: true` in the merged stage source

The pre-fold `compose-contributions.ts` parsed both entries with correct flags, so this is a regression from the fold, and it fires on every compose of the reference plugin. Downstream, aidlc-graph's consume validation (`if (!consume.required) continue;`) then subjects the optional consume to producer validation. t188 only asserts `toContain` of the first artifact, so the suite cannot see either defect; please also assert the second artifact and the required flag.

Fixed in `7c00c7f`. The consumes parser is rewritten to parse each entry as a block (`- artifact:` plus its indented `required:`/`conditional_on:` continuation lines), not by zipping two independent artifact/required scans. So every entry lands (not just the first), and `required` is read per-entry — an authored `required: false` is preserved rather than flipped. Verified against the shipped build-and-test fixture: both test-pro consumes merge with `required: false` intact. t188 now asserts the 2nd artifact **and** the required flag (and that core's `code-generation-plan` stays `required: true`).

**[MAJOR, latent] mergeConsumes corrupts conditional_on stages.**

This blockRe has no `conditional_on` branch, so appending a consume to any of the 5 core stages whose consumes end with `conditional_on: brownfield` (practices-discovery, user-stories, application-design, requirements-analysis, nfr-requirements) splices the new entry before the conditional_on line: the core artifact silently loses its brownfield gate and the plugin's artifact gains it. Reproduced with the real engine parse+validate: the corrupted result validates clean, persists in stage source, and the artifact-name idempotence check means it is never repaired.

Not fired by the shipped fixture (its `adds.consumes` target build-and-test and nfr-design), but armed for any third-party plugin. One-line fix: `(?:    (?:required|conditional_on):.*\n)*` in the entry alternative.

Fixed in `7c00c7f`. The consumes blockRe now matches `conditional_on` continuation lines: `(?:    (?:required|conditional_on):.*\n)*`. So appending to a stage whose consumes end in `conditional_on: brownfield` (the 5 core stages you named) captures the whole block and appends AFTER it — the core artifact keeps its brownfield gate and the plugin's entry doesn't inherit it. Reproduced the fix directly on a conditional_on-terminated block.

**[MINOR, non-blocking - follow-up PR is fine] Cross-file same-key fragments silently last-writer-win; the docs still promise a build error.**

The intra-file collision drops-with-log now (good), but the same (bundle, anchor, order) key arriving from two contribution files takes this upgrade path instead: the hash differs, so the second file's prose replaces the first with no drop, and the winner is decided by readdir order of the phase dirs. 10-authoring-a-plugin.md line 175 and 18-plugin-mechanism.md line 184 still describe this as a build error. Either extend the drop-log to the cross-file case or align both doc claims with drop-with-log semantics.

Done in `54faa29` (not deferred). A run-wide seen-set now keys `(target, bundle, anchor, order)` across ALL contribution files, so a same-key fragment arriving from a second file drops-with-log rather than taking the hash-upgrade path (which was silent, readdir-order-decided). Cross-RUN upgrades still work (fresh process → empty seen-set → hash path). Aligned the doc claims in doc 18 and 10-authoring with drop-with-log semantics.

This picks the LAST `STAGE_AWAITING_APPROVAL` for the slug with no filter on `Recovered`. That's the false-negative: when the conductor skipped the optional organic gate-start, the stage is `[-]`, so report auto-injects `gate-start --recovered` before approve (orchestrate.ts:2776) as a separate spawn. Its synthesized AWAITING row gets a fresh timestamp *after* the revision and human turns, becomes the anchor here, and the conjunct-3 scan from `anchor+1` then finds no HUMAN_TURN (`firstHuman === -1`) — so the predicate returns false and the revision goes unrecorded. Skip `Recovered=true` rows when choosing the anchor, or anchor on the real gate boundary (prior GATE resolution / STAGE_STARTED), so the pre-anchor human turn + revision stay in the window.

Double-count on the nested path. When called as `scanSignals(sub, 1)`, this line already counts files directly under `<sub>/src`, `<sub>/app`, etc. at depth 1 — then the loop just below recurses those same `SCAN_SOURCE_DIRS` dirs again at depth 6, so files directly under them are counted twice. The root call (`scanSignals(dir, 0)`) is immune because the depth-0 sweep never enters subdirs.

Effect: the `Languages` field can name the wrong primary language for a nested project (e.g. 3 `.ts` under `src/` doubled to 6 beats 4 top-level `.py`). Classification is fine (boolean OR), but that wrong value is written to aidlc-state.md, the WORKSPACE_SCANNED audit, and `detect --json`.

Fix: exclude `SCAN_SOURCE_DIRS` names from the depth-1 sweep so the depth-6 recurse is the only counter, mirroring the root path.

This filters `node.produces` by kind but drops the `[...produces, ...optional_produces]` concat that #509 (optional_produces, already on v2) added here — so an optional artifact never reaches the directive. And `frontend-components`, which #509 moved into `optional_produces`, is what `produces_kinds: {frontend-components: [ui]}` maps: since the filter only reads `node.produces`, that mapping is dead and a `ui` unit never gets it (same for `shared-infrastructure`). Filter the combined list instead: `filterProducesByKind(node.produces_kinds, [...(node.produces ?? []), ...(node.optional_produces ?? [])], unitKind)`, and keep the kind map pointed at whichever list holds the artifact. `unitCovered` needs the matching treatment (kind-filter the required list, keep optional exempt from coverage per #509).
